chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated: Husayn ibn Ali al-Rawasi attended the funeral of Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

When the body was placed by the edge of the grave, a messenger from Sandi ibn Shahik arrived and said to Aba al-Muda, his deputy (who was with the funeral procession): 'Expose his face to the people before you bury him, so that they may see him healthy, that no new event (injury/torture) has happened to him.' He said: 'They uncovered the face of my Master, so I saw him and recognized him, then his face was covered and he was placed in his grave, may God's blessings be upon him.'

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The kunya (honorific name) of Imam Musa al-Kadim (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الرُّوَاسِي: A nisba indicating belonging to Rawas, a place or tribe associated with Husayn ibn Ali.
key_terms.سَنْدِيٌّ بْنِ شَاهِكَ: A prominent companion and official, Sandi ibn Shahik.
key_terms.صَحِيحًا: Healthy, intact, free from major defects or injuries.
key_terms.لَمْ يُحْدَثْ بِهِ حَدَثٌ: That no new event/incident (such as torture or injury) had occurred to him.

ai.seo_question: How did the companions verify the cause of Imam Kadim's death before burial?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* details the burial of Imam Musa al-Kadim (AS) in Egypt, emphasizing the political anxiety of the Abbasid governor Sandi ibn Shahik regarding the Imam's cause of death. By exposing the Imam's face to the public, the authorities sought to verify that he died naturally rather than from torture, thereby legitimizing their narrative and preventing rumors of assassination.
